captions.caption: Attention in word and design. Left: A Dream, Songs copy Y, plate 26 (Met 17.10.26), whose vegetation runs around and between the stanzas; a small upright figure at lower right remains uncertain in this reading. Right: The Fly, copy Y, plate 40 (17.10.40), with a large figure supporting a child's raised hands and another figure playing with a racket and shuttlecock-like object. The visible human scene offers an analogy with the named fly without supplying a resolved zoological portrait. William Blake, printed ca.1825; The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1917. Public Domain / Open Access. Whole captured scans proportionally resized; not shown at equal physical scale. Each panel is also supplied as a separate whole-plate derivative.

Forms of injury and entanglement. Left: The Sick Rose, Songs copy Y, plate 39 (Met 17.10.39), with thorned vegetation, small bent figures and an exposed lower body beside an ambiguous narrow bent form. Right: The Human Abstract, copy Y, plate 47 (17.10.47), with an aged figure raising his arms among cord-like forms. The worm of the first poem and the feeding caterpillar and fly of the second belong to different rhetorical situations; these designs do not settle their biological identities. William Blake, printed ca.1825; The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Rogers Fund, 1917. Public Domain / Open Access. Whole captured scans proportionally resized; separate full-page versions supplied.

One plate in two material witnesses. The Book of Thel, Bentley plate 6 (Erdman plate 4): left, copy F object6, LOC Rosenwald1798A; right, copy O object5, LOC digital resource Rosenwald1798B. The floating, standing and infant-like figures retain their etched arrangement, while the reproduced gowns, washes and painted enclosure differ. The nearby text calls the infant-like figure the Worm; no taxon is inferred from this analogy. Archive print dates are 1795 and c.1818; LOC catalogue descriptions give ca.1794 and ca.1815 respectively. The disagreement is retained. William Blake; Library of Congress, Rare Book and Special Collections Division, Lessing J. Rosenwald Collection. Historical public-domain artwork, LOC no-known-US-restrictions statement. Proportional whole-scan resizing only; photographic colour and physical scales are not calibrated.

Care beyond the prohibition of injury. The Book of Thel, copy O, object6, Bentley plate7 (Erdman plate5), LOC digital Rosenwald1798B. A reclining adult-like figure reaches towards an infant-like figure beneath the exchange in which Thel distinguishes punishment of a bruising foot from positive nurture with milk and oil. The lower scene is read with the selected Clay/Worm text, not as a zoological specimen. William Blake; Library of Congress, Rare Book and Special Collections Division, Lessing J. Rosenwald Collection. Archive dates this printing c.1818; LOC catalogue gives ca.1815. Historical public-domain artwork; whole captured scan proportionally resized.
